title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. C2-C8 are out of scope for this plan because they require 12 datasets and would take hours; the code is dataset-agnostic if extended.

"""Proximity kernel implementation following the paper exactly."""
import numpy as np
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional, Tuple, List, Dict


@dataclass
class ProximityKernelResult:
    Z: np.ndarray  # (n, d * nbins) representation
    bin_centers: np.ndarray  # (d, nbins)
    bin_assignments: np.ndarray  # (n, d), -1 for missing
    global_priors: np.ndarray  # (d, nbins)
    level1_count: int
    level2_count: int
    level3_count: int
    total_missing: int
    diagnostics: Dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def _equal_frequency_centers(obs: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Compute equal-frequency bin centers using evenly-spaced percentiles.
    Paper Eq. (4): c_{j,k} = percentile(X_{obs,j}, (k-1) * 100 / (nbins-1))
    """
    if len(obs) == 0:
        return np.full(nbins, np.nan)
    
    # Percentiles: (k-1) * 100 / (nbins-1) for k = 1..nbins
    percentiles = np.arange(nbins) * 100.0 / (nbins - 1)
    centers = np.percentile(obs, percentiles, method="linear")
    return centers


def _proximity_assign(x: float, centers: np.ndarray) -> int:
    """Assign observed value to nearest bin center."""
    if np.isnan(centers).any():
        return -1
    dists = np.abs(x - centers)
    return int(np.argmin(dists))


def fit_bins(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Fit bin centers for each feature.
    Returns:
        centers: (d, nbins) array of bin centers
        global_priors: (d, nbins) array of global prior probabilities
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    centers = np.full((d, nbins), np.nan)
    global_priors = np.zeros((d, nbins))
    
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if len(obs) > 0:
            centers[j] = _equal_frequency_centers(obs, nbins)
            # Compute global priors from observed values only
            assignments = np.array([_proximity_assign(v, centers[j]) for v in obs])
            for k in range(nbins):
                global_priors[j, k] = np.sum(assignments == k) / len(obs)
        else:
            # Feature entirely missing: uniform prior
            centers[j] = np.linspace(0, 1, nbins)
            global_priors[j] = 1.0 / nbins
    
    return centers, global_priors


def assign_bins(X: np.ndarray, centers: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Assign each observed value to its nearest bin center."""
    n, d = X.shape
    nbins = centers.shape[1]
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(d):
            if not np.isnan(X[i, j]):
                B[i, j] = _proximity_assign(X[i, j], centers[j])
    
    return B


def encode_observed(B: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Create one-hot encodings for observed bin assignments."""
    n, d = B.shape
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins))
    
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(d):
            if B[i, j] >= 0:
                H[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1.0
    
    return H


def compute_fallback_encodings(
    X: np.ndarray,
    B: np.ndarray,
    H_obs: np.ndarray,
    centers: np.ndarray,
    global_priors: np.ndarray,
    nbins: int
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, int, int, int]:
    """
    Compute missing feature encodings using three-level cascading fallback.
    Returns:
        H: (n, d, nbins) full encodings
        level1_count, level2_count, level3_count
    """
    n, d = B.shape
    H = H_obs.copy()
    level1_count = 0
    level2_count = 0
    level3_count = 0
    
    for i in range(n):
        O_i = [j for j in range(d) if B[i, j] >= 0]
        M_i = [j for j in range(d) if B[i, j] < 0]
        
        if not M_i:
            continue
        
        # Level 1: Intersection-based matching
        S1 = None
        if O_i:
            S1 = set(range(n)) - {i}
            for j in O_i:
                C_ij = {m for m in range(n) if m != i and B[m, j] == B[i, j]}
                S1 = S1 & C_ij
        
        # Level 2: Union-based matching
        S2 = None
        if O_i:
            S2 = set()
            for j in O_i:
                C_ij = {m for m in range(n) if m != i and B[m, j] == B[i, j]}
                S2 = S2 | C_ij

                H[i, j] = vals.mean(axis=0)
                level1_count += 1
            # Try Level 2
            elif S2 is not None and len(S2) > 0:
                vals = np.array([H_obs[m, j] for m in S2])
                H[i, j] = vals.mean(axis=0)
                level2_count += 1
            # Level 3: Global prior
            else:
                H[i, j] = global_priors[j].copy()
                level3_count += 1
    
    return H, level1_count, level2_count, level3_count


def build_representation(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> ProximityKernelResult:
    """
    Build the proximity kernel representation for dataset X.
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    
    # Step 1: Fit bins
    centers, global_priors = fit_bins(X, nbins)
    
    # Step 2: Assign bins
    B = assign_bins(X, centers)
    
    # Step 3: Encode observed values
    H_obs = encode_observed(B, nbins)

        X, B, H_obs, centers, global_priors, nbins
    )
    
    # Step 5: Concatenate across features to get Z

        level2_count=level2_count,
        level3_count=level3_count,

def evaluate_nbins(
    X: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    K: int,
    nbins: int,
    seeds: list
) -> dict:
    """
    Evaluate proximity kernel with a given nbins value.
    Returns mean, std, and per-seed NMI scores.
    """
    result = build_representation(X, nbins)
    Z = result.Z
    d = X.shape[1]
    
    # Verify no NaN/inf in Z
    assert not np.isnan(Z).any(), "Z contains NaN"
    assert not np.isinf(Z).any(), "Z contains inf"
    
    # Verify encodings sum to 1 per feature
    n, D = Z.shape
    Z_reshaped = Z.reshape(n, d, nbins)
    feature_sums = Z_reshaped.sum(axis=2)
    assert np.allclose(feature_sums, 1.0, atol=1e-6), "Feature encodings do not sum to 1"
    
    # Verify kernel properties
    K_mat = proximity_kernel(Z, d)
    assert np.allclose(K_mat, K_mat.T), "Kernel matrix not symmetric"
    assert np.all(K_mat.diagonal() <= 1.0 + 1e-6), "Kernel diagonal > 1"
    assert np.all(K_mat >= -1e-6) and np.all(K_mat <= 1.0 + 1e-6), "Kernel values out of [0,1]"
    
    nmis = []
    for seed in seeds:
        kmeans = KMeans(
            n_clusters=K,
            init="k-means++",
            n_init=10,
            random_state=seed
        )
        labels = kmeans.fit_predict(Z)
        nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels)
        nmis.append(nmi)
    
    nmis = np.array(nmis)
    return {
        "nbins": nbins,
        "mean_nmi": float(nmis.mean()),
        "std_nmi": float(nmis.std()),
        "min_nmi": float(nmis.min()),

        "per_seed": {int(s): float(v) for s, v in zip(seeds, nmis)},
        "level1_count": result.level1_count,
        "level2_count": result.level2_count,
        "level3_count": result.level3_count,
        "total_missing": result.total_missing,
        "missing_rate": result.diagnostics["missing_rate"],
    }

    For each missing entry (i, j), the mean is taken over matching samples
    that actually have feature j observed (S1_j / S2_j), normalized by that count.
    Returns:

The dataset is the genuine UCI Hepatitis file (155x19, classes [32,123], 167 missing = 5.67%), matching Table 2. right_experiment is true: same dataset, split family (transductive full-data clustering), metric (NMI) and method (the proposed kernel, not a baseline). No scale-down occurred (full dataset, all 5 nbins, all 10 seeds); the median-imputation baseline is used only as a sanity check. The reported value 0.2289091446 (diff 9e-6 from target 0.2289) is genuinely computed from KMeans+, not hardcoded; the literal 0.2289 in reproduce.py is only the comparison target. Caveats: (1) the percentile-position choice (endpoints 0/100 for nbins=2, i.e. min/max as centers) is a specific reading of the underspecified Eq.(4) that does not produce true equal-frequency bins after nearest-center assignment, and it is not covered by the assumption ledger (A2 only fixes the interpolation method); (2) std=0.0 across the 10 seeds means the average is effectively one deterministic partition, so the perfect 4-decimal match to the paper is partly a coincidence of a highly stable clustering; neither issue evidences hardcoding, but the exact match should be treated with mild caution.

requirement_check.evidence: fit_bins() computes bin centers only from observed entries (obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:,j]), j]) and assigns every observed value; missing entries are handled separately by the fallback. No imputation is used to build centers.

_equal_frequency_centers uses percentiles = arange(nbins)*100/(nbins-1), i.e. for nbins=2 centers are the 0th and 100th percentiles (min/max) and for nbins=3 [0,50,100]. These are literally 'evenly-spaced percentiles' with linear interpolation (A2), but using the extreme percentiles as centers does not yield truly equal-frequency bins after nearest-center assignment. The paper's Eq.(4) is underspecified on the percentile positions, so this is a defensible but non-unique reading.
_proximity_assign uses argmin(|x - c|) over the feature's centers; ties fall to the lowest index (A3).
encode_observed builds H of shape (n,d,nbins) with a single 1 per observed feature, then Z=H.reshape(n,d*nbins) concatenates features (Eqs. 6-7).
compute_fallback_encodings implements the three-level cascade: Level-1 intersection S1, Level-2 union S2, Level-3 global prior, tracking level1/2/3 counts.
When S1_j is nonempty the code sets H[i,j]=mean of H_obs[m,j] over m in S1_j, restricted to matching samples that observed feature j (assumption A8, a reasonable non-recursive reading of Eq.10).
If no intersection match, S2_j = {m in union matching any observed feature, with feature j observed} is used for the mean (Eqs.11-12).
If S1_j and S2_j are both empty, H[i,j]=global_priors[j], the empirical bin-frequency prior per feature (Eqs.13-14); fully-missing features get uniform prior (A7).
proximity_kernel returns Z @ Z.T / d, and evaluate_nbins asserts symmetry and [0,1] range (Eq.15).
evaluate_nbins uses sklearn KMeans(n_clusters=K ground-truth) on Z and normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); K=2 for Hepatitis.

10 seeds (0-9) are averaged; per-seed NMIs are logged. Note std=0.0 because the deterministic kernel + n_init=10 KMeans gives identical partitions across seeds, so it is effectively a single deterministic run.
nbins_grid=[2,3,4,6,8] is searched; best picked by mean NMI (A9).
Time-complexity claim not tested; no scaling-in-n experiment was run (only a single 155-sample fit). This is tangential to target C1.
For fully observed samples each feature row is a strict one-hot (feature_sums asserted to equal 1), i.e. exactly d ones out of d*nbins; fractional means appear only for imputed missing entries.
